newsitem.title: USA: Scholastic stock tumbles after loss forecast.
newsitem.headline: Scholastic stock tumbles after loss forecast.

text.p: Scholastic Corp.'s stock lost 40 percent of its value Friday, a day after the children's book publisher warned of a third-quarter loss and a decline in fiscal year earnings.

The sell-off was hastened as major Wall Street brokerages, including Merrill Lynch & Co., UBS Securities and Smith Barney, downgraded the stock and cut earnings estimates for the publisher of the well known magazine, books and other educational products.

The stock, which hit a high of $78.50 in the last year, tumbled $24.75 to close at $36.75 on Nasdaq, where it was the second biggest loser and one of the most active issues. Volume was about 4.3 million shares, 14 times the daily average.

After the market closed on Thursday, Scholastic said it expected a loss of 70 to 80 cents a share in its fiscal third quarter ending Feb. 28. This includes 50 cents a share for reserves taken for returns by retailers.
The New York-based company earned $8.9 million, or 55 cents a share, on revenues of $216.1 million in the year-ago third quarter.
Scholastic also said it expected earnings of $1.45 to $1.60 a share for the year ending on May 31, below the $1.97 a share posted last year.
Scholastic cited a drop in shipments of older titles in its "Goosebumps" children's book series and costs to promote its "Literacy Place" reading programme.
Scholastic said it was committed to cutting costs it could without hurting revenues.

UBS Securities analyst Edward Hatch said Scholastic held a conference call with analysts soon after the announcement to "detail a dramatic and unforeseen shortfall in trade book sales at its major 'Goosebumps' franchise.
"In addition, an expected sales revival at its core book club business in the second half of fiscal ... 1997 has now been pushed out to fiscal 1998," Hatch said in a research note.
He suggested the company seemed late to realise and report the sales trouble, calling into question "the veracity of its systems and response time in learning problems."
Two Wall Street firms recommended selling Scholastic stock.
Merrill Lynch slashed its near-term recommendation to "reduce" from accumulate, while Deutsche Morgan Grenfell declared the stock a "sell," down from "hold."
Deutsche Morgan analyst Rudolf Hokanson said that Goosebumps was still a very valuable brand but that sales slowed so dramatically, according to management, that it was "frightening."
Management now expects fiscal 1998 earnings to be $2.25 to $2.75 a share, Hokanson said, referring to comments made by the company in last night's conference call.
"At some point every stock can become a value. Scholastic's stock could conceivably trade well below $40 per share in our opinion and may still not be attractive," he wrote.
Added UBS's Hatch, "Long-term, this is an excellent franchise and there may be interest by value investors after the dust settles."
